newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe - would implement tax measures within six mths.
newsitem.headline: Juppe - would implement tax measures within six mths.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday that he would implement tax measures within the first six months of the new legislature if the centre-right coalition returns to power after the May 25/June 1 election.

The measures, which include cutting payroll charges for small companies in low wage sectors, would be applied "either in the first 40 days, or in the first six months, to lighten the load on those who work in this country".
"The emphasis should from now on be on economic growth through the reduction of taxes and charges," Juppe said on Europe 1 radio.

On the reduction of payroll charges for small firms in low wage sectors, Juppe said the plan was to allow cuts in the public works, retail and footwear sectors along the lines already applied in the textiles sector.

He said sickness insurance contributions would be cut for wage earners via a transfer to the CSG levy, a one-off tax on most personal income, but on a lesser scale than that proposed by the opposition Socialist party.

"Mr (Socialist party leader Lionel) Jospin has made a proposal which is not serious, raising the CSG to eight percent, which is excessive. We are proposing a transfer to the tune of two percentage points," Juppe said.
The CSG levy currently stands at 3.40 percent.
The government would continue with its already announced five-year plan for income tax worth a total 75 billion francs. That plan was part of its 1996 budget, Juppe said.
He also said the government would like to go further in reducing taxes on small companies and local company taxes.
